I am a bit conflicted by this article, as in I am not sure whether this is an acceptable practice or not.

The purpose of a patent is to secure - for the duration of the patent - the singular supplier of the protected article. This means that a patent holder gets to decide who can produce the article. For example, Apple patents the iPhone shape, and thus Apple only gets to make it. Or, Ford produces an integrated dashboard, and Ford gets to decide who it licenses to and allows to add to their automobiles.

Working without a patent is ENTIRELY allowed. And this is the source of my confusion.

If I were to develop a technology that is innovative, and apply for a patent, but the government says 'that patent must be secret' - there is nothing (that I am aware of, which could be my confusion) that says I cannot just make the damn thing and try to sell it.
